intro: Tap a drum. Feel the buzz under your hand. Hear the boom. Turn off the lamp. The room goes dark. Your shadow is gone. Sound and light are all around you, every day. This unit is about both of them.

You will find out what a sound really is. It is a wiggle. Something shakes, and the shake spreads to your ear. You will find out what light does. It shines from the sun or a bulb. It bounces off things and into your eyes.
By the end, you can explain a drum. Why does it stop when you touch it? You can explain a shadow. Why does it move? And you can send a secret message. Use claps, or blinks of a flashlight.
bigQuestion: How do sound and light get from a drum or a lamp to you, and how can they carry a message?

timeline.t: An alarm buzzes. Something inside it is shaking fast. That shake is the sound.
Light comes in the window. Now you can see your room. The sun is a light source.
A spoon clinks on a bowl. The bowl vibrates. The sound spreads through the air.
Your shadow is long on the sidewalk. The sun is low in the sky.
Hand on the drum bench. Feel the buzz. Loud hits make big wiggles.
A whistle blows. Everyone stops. The sound carried a message.
Shadows are very short now. The sun is high overhead.
You look through a window. Glass lets light through. The wall does not.
A ship horn sounds on the lake in the fog. The horn says: I am here.
The lighthouse beam turns on. Its light tells boats where the shore is.
You blink a flashlight to your sister. Two blinks mean no, one means yes.
Lights off. The room is dark. You cannot see, but you can still hear.

words.d: a very fast shaking back and forth
a sound that is big and strong, easy to hear
a sound like a bird chirp or a whistle
to move from one place to another
what lets your eyes see; it comes from the sun, fire and bulbs
a thing that makes its own light, like the sun or a bulb
a dark spot made when something blocks light
a smooth shiny surface that bounces light back

test.q: Where does a sound come from?
test.why: Every sound starts with a vibration, a fast shake. The shake spreads to your ear.

test.q: You press your hand on a ringing drum. The sound:
test.why: Your hand stops the skin from shaking. No shaking means no sound.
A big drum shakes slowly. Slow shaking makes a low sound.

test.q: Rice on a drum hops when you clap. What moved the rice?
choices: The sound shaking the drum skin
test.why: The clap sound spread through the air and shook the drum. The rice hopped.
Sound travels through air, through water and through solids like a table.

test.q: What do your eyes need to see?
test.why: Eyes only work when light reaches them. In a dark room you see nothing.

test.q: Which one makes its own light?
test.why: A flashlight is a light source. Rocks and books only bounce light.

choices: A dark spot where light is blocked
test.why: When something blocks light, the place behind it stays dark. That is the shadow.

test.q: What does a mirror do to light?
test.why: A mirror is smooth and shiny. Light bounces off it, so you see your face.

test.q: Which is a message sent with light?
test.why: A lighthouse sends its message with light. Bells and whistles use sound.

write.prompt: Pick one: sound or light. Make a claim: how does it get from where it starts to you? Use two things you saw in this unit as evidence. Then tell why your evidence proves your claim.
tips: Claim: say your idea in one short sentence.
Evidence: use the drum and the rice, or the lamp and the shadow.
Reasoning: tell why your evidence shows your claim is true.
Other side: what might a friend say? Why are they wrong?
